items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: Vic played music like Fanny Brown, Wynonie Harris, music, of the so-called race music of the early 50s.

ctx.x: So they would have been playing—

Vic played music like Fanny Brown, Wynonie Harris, music, of the so-called race music of the early 50s. And the Utica kids ate it up. And I went in and he had this fabulous rhythm section. Gordon Smith was truly a great drummer. And he had lived, he had a heart defect and died Labor Day of 1959. I think he was 28. But if he had lived and had come to New York, which is where he was born, he really was a great drummer. To me his level of accomplishment, artistically, was that of an Arthur Taylor or Philly Joe even.…
fairly unique, not unlike an Elvin Jones or a Philly Joe. And he was pretty wise for his age too. He seemed old to me then, I was 17 then or 16. But he taught me things about life and music as well.
